If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over last 5 days, reduce forecast peak by 1–2% in mid-horizon (days 15–25) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over last 5 days, increase forecast trough by 1–2% in early-horizon (days 1–10) to compensate for pessimism.  
When sentiment spikes to 1.00 on day 1–3, adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% for next 3 days to reflect market correction.  
If sentiment shifts from high to low within 3 days, reduce forecast slope in mid-horizon by 0.5–1.0% to reflect sentiment reversal.  
In late-horizon (days 25–30), if sentiment remains stable at 0.5–0.67, apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias to avoid overextension.  
If sentiment is high but price is trending down, reduce forecast by 1–2% in late-horizon to align with sentiment-driven volatility.
